newsitem.title: USA: HSBC James Capel ups Brazil, Chile, cuts Mexico.
newsitem.headline: HSBC James Capel ups Brazil, Chile, cuts Mexico.

text.p: HSBC James Capel said on Monday it had raised Brazil and Chile to overweight from underweight in its model portfolio of Latin American stocks.
In a report, analysts Geoffrey Dennis and Scott Schwager also cut Mexico to neutral from overweight.
They also raised Venezuela to neutral from underweight and cut Argentina and Peru to underweight from overweight.
Dennis and Schwager wrote that investors should "downplay those markets (such as Argentina and Mexico) where an unexpected U.S. (interest) rate increase would have the greatest relative impact.
"In turn, (investors should) favor those major markets (such as Chile and Brazil) where higher U.S. rates would have the least impact."
Investors also should "increase weightings in some of the underperforming markets of 1996, notably Chile and Colombia, but not Peru."
They cut the relative weighting of Argentina to eight from 12 percent, of Mexico to 29.6 from 31 percent and Peru to 2.3 from 3.8 percent.
Brazil's weighting was raised to 36.5 from 32.7 percent, Chile's to 17.7 from 16 percent and Venezuela's to 2.2 from 0.6 percent. Colombia went to 3.7 from 3.9 percent.
